clue.text: Exhaust dog with constant exercise

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them, to tail them
pi is the best-known mathematical constant
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone tires out their dog with a steady fitness routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhaust' reads as a verb about wearing the dog out, but it is a noun naming part of a car; 'dog' is a verb meaning follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipe at the back of a car that carries away engine fumes is called its exhaust.

clue.text: Wireless broadcast on air distorts artist being showcased

indicators.note: something showcased sits inside a display case, so one piece is set within the other
seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
an RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist

explanation.surface: A radio broadcast twists the work of an artist who is being promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distorts' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the letters to be mixed; 'broadcast' does the mixing. RA (Royal Academician) is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Wireless is the old British word for a radio set, and a small portable one built with transistors fits it.

clue.text: Ripon's unrestricted, expanded inaugural sale of stock

indicators.note: with no restrictions, the bounds at either end are lifted, so only the inside letters stay

parts.note: Ripon, a cathedral city in North Yorkshire, without its outer letters
the abbreviation written out in full

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire firm from Ripon, freed of limits and grown, puts its shares on sale for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: IPO is a standard financial abbreviation; 'expanded' asks for it to be spelt out word by word.
explanation.definitionFit: When a company first offers its shares to the public on a stock exchange, the event goes by this formal term.

clue.text: Herald regularly spurned flashing light on computer screen

indicators.note: doing something regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters
the blinking marker showing where typing will appear

explanation.surface: A newspaper keeps ignoring a blinking light on someone's monitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herald' looks like a newspaper title, but it is a noun meaning a forerunner.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald announces what is coming, just as a forerunner arrives before the main event or person.

clue.text: See 2
Trade tax spat involving alpha Republican

indicators.note: to involve is to take in or include, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: a spat is a minor quarrel
alpha is the NATO alphabet word for A
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A row about import duties draws in a dominant Republican politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alpha' suggests an alpha male, but it is just the letter A from the phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a duty charged by a government on imported or exported goods.

clue.text: Use American ski resort in The Rockies

parts.note: standard abbreviation
Vail is a ski resort in Colorado

explanation.surface: An invitation to make use of a US ski resort in the Rocky Mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: Vail is a well-known Colorado ski town, the kind of American place name solvers are expected to know.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, avail means benefit or usefulness, as in 'to no avail', matching use in the sense of value.

clue.text: Area including French overseas department's promoting island lizards

indicators.note: to promote is to move up, and in a down clue up means towards the front

parts.note: standard abbreviation
Guiana is the South American region that includes French Guiana, with the 's added

explanation.surface: A French overseas territory boosts an island's reptile population.
explanation.walkthrough: The I of GUIANAS moves up to the top of the word; French Guiana is an overseas department of France on the north coast of South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Iguanas are large tropical lizards found across Central and South America and the Caribbean.

clue.text: Florida Keys rip-off stealing women's showy sparklers?

indicators.note: a thief takes something into keeping, so one piece is drawn inside the others
food that is off has gone bad, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A con in the Florida Keys involves stealing women's flashy diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rip-off' reads as one word for a swindle, but it splits: 'rip' joins the letters to be mixed and 'off' mixes them. Sparklers suggests diamonds here.
explanation.definitionFit: A pyrotechnic show is literally a flashy collection of things that sparkle; the question mark flags the playful reading.

clue.text: In which people attempt to reduce stress when 2 4 goes badly?

definitions.text: In which people attempt to reduce stress

parts.note: the answer to 2/4 is a company's first sale of shares, also called this
a venture that tanks fails badly

explanation.surface: People try to calm down when a share launch collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: A company's stock-market debut is called a flotation in British usage, so the cross-reference gives a synonym rather than its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: These are enclosed pods of warm salt water where people lie weightless for relaxation therapy, so they are places used for calming.

clue.text: Quick! Area 51 base invaded by leader of Vulcans!

indicators.note: an invaded territory has forces inside it, so a letter enters the other pieces

parts.note: standard abbreviation
51 in Roman numerals is L (50) plus I (1)
e is the base of natural logarithms

indicators.note: the leader is at the front, so only an opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: An urgent alarm: Spock's people are attacking the secret US airbase.
explanation.walkthrough: Area 51 is a secret US base, but here it splits into area and a Roman number. 'Quick' is the old sense in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: In older English, quick meant living, as in the phrase about judging both the living and the dead.

clue.text: Dembélé, Agüero defending attack from all sides

indicators.note: defenders surround and guard what they protect, so the answer sits held inside these words

parts.note: runs across the two footballers' names, ignoring accents

explanation.surface: Two star footballers, Ousmane Dembélé and Sergio Agüero, defending against an all-round assault.
explanation.walkthrough: The accents on the players' names are ignored, as is usual in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To beleaguer is to besiege, surrounding a place with an army so it is under pressure everywhere.

clue.text: Second time Knut's university starts to limit inoculations (shots in the arm)

parts.note: standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation
the setter speaking of himself: Knut is = I am, I'm
standard abbreviation

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only opening letters are taken

parts.note: the first letters of each

explanation.surface: The setter returns to university to curb vaccinations, with a pun on jabs in the arm.
explanation.walkthrough: When a setter names himself, 'Knut's' means 'Knut is', which the solver turns into I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot in the arm is an idiom for a boost or encouragement, which is what stimuli provide.

clue.text: Order to ploughman to work up to this point

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an instruction to cultivate the soil at once

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a command, the phrase tells a farmer to start ploughing immediately; read as a phrase, it means hitherto.
explanation.definitionFit: Together the two words mean so far in time, a common phrase for everything up to the present moment.

clue.text: Bet against Stroll — he's all over the place

indicators.note: something all over the place is scattered and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wager on Lance Stroll, the erratic Formula One driver, failing.
explanation.walkthrough: Stroll looks like a verb but is the driver's name, with a capital to hide it as letter fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell short is a stock-market move that profits when a price falls, effectively wagering that it will drop.

clue.text: Question Time deleted from advertising placard

indicators.note: deleting removes something, so a letter is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: a poster is a printed notice put up for advertising
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: The BBC debate show Question Time is axed from a billboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make 'Question Time' look like the TV programme title, but the words split into the definition and a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling or awkward question that is hard to answer.

clue.text: Affirm cider is being served up with terrine outside

indicators.note: something outside goes around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: pâté is a terrine-like meat or fish paste

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means set upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confirms the cider is poured to go with a terrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served up' sounds like a waiter at work, but in a down answer it turns letters upward.
explanation.definitionFit: To predicate is to state or assert something as a property of a subject, so it means to declare firmly.

clue.text: Mum's dumping Mike for somebody else

indicators.note: dumping something throws it away, so a letter is discarded

parts.note: mum is an informal word for mother
Mike is the NATO alphabet word for M

explanation.surface: A mother is leaving her partner Mike for another man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum's' means 'Mum is', so the deletion runs on the longer word for a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: The other is a different person from the one mentioned, a pronoun use for someone apart.

clue.text: Partially exhume Russian body part

indicators.note: only a part of the words is used, so the answer lies within a stretch of them

parts.note: runs from the second letter of the verb into the adjective

explanation.surface: Digging up part of a Russian corpse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body part' seems to continue the grave-robbing story, but it is the definition, a bone sitting inside the opening words.
explanation.definitionFit: The humerus is the long bone of the upper arm, running from shoulder to elbow.

clue.text: Flared trousers open, almost entirely like Droopy?

indicators.note: nearly all of a word is used, so its last letter is dropped
used as a verb, to trouser is to pocket something, so one piece is tucked inside another

parts.note: taken as written
the word without its final letter

explanation.surface: Bell-bottom trousers hanging open, looking almost exactly like a droopy cartoon character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flared trousers' reads as a garment, but 'trousers' is a verb meaning pockets. Droopy is a lugubrious basset-hound cartoon dog with hanging ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Having ears that hang down limply describes the famous sad-faced cartoon hound, hence the question mark for an example.

clue.text: VAR overturned goal slashing the odds in 1-1 Italian classic

indicators.note: a decision overturned is flipped, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written: the video assistant referee in football

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: one and one as Roman numerals

indicators.note: cutting out the odd positions leaves only the even-numbered letters

parts.note: second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A video review reverses a goal, cutting the bookmakers' prices in a draw between Italian giants.
explanation.walkthrough: The football surface hides a pasta: the 1-1 scoreline is two Roman ones, with the remains of 'goal' between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli, small filled pasta parcels, are a traditional dish of Italian cooking.

clue.text: One who doesn't mind being told to take a hike?

definitions.text: One who doesn't mind being told to take a hike?

parts.words: One who doesn't mind being told to take a hike?
parts.note: surface reading: a thick-skinned person unbothered by being told rudely to go away; setter's reading: someone who loves country walks is happy to be sent on one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Take a hike' is a dismissive phrase meaning get lost, but taken literally it is an invitation a keen walker would welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a rambler is a person who walks in the countryside for pleasure, so a long hike suits them.

clue.text: Exit the Parisian boulevard

parts.note: le is French for the
short for avenue, a broad street

explanation.surface: A sign for the way out onto a Paris boulevard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Parisian' asks for the French word for 'the', the masculine article.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit and to leave are synonymous verbs for going out of a place.

clue.text: Burglars this evening staying in?

indicators.note: staying in means remaining inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: taken as written
eve is a poetic word for evening

explanation.surface: A worried question: are the burglars coming tonight while we are at home?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staying in' sounds like a cosy night at home, but it puts the short word for evening inside 'this', after its I.
explanation.definitionFit: Burglars break into buildings to steal, so they are a particular kind of robber.

clue.text: Temperature in Granada bothered knight, a dashing blade

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it
something bothered is agitated and stirred up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
standard abbreviation
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Heat in the Spanish city of Granada troubles a gallant swordsman.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in D'Artagnan is ignored. In chess notation K is the king, so the knight is N.
explanation.definitionFit: D'Artagnan is the swashbuckling swordsman hero of Dumas's The Three Musketeers, and a blade is a dashing young man.

clue.text: Bikini? Perhaps Lolita doesn't need one

indicators.note: perhaps signals one possible version, so the remaining letters are rearranged
what is not needed can be thrown out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
one as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A swimsuit question about Nabokov's young heroine, who apparently goes without.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bikini' wants to be the swimsuit, but it is Bikini Atoll in the Pacific, scene of US nuclear tests; the question mark marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini is a ring-shaped coral reef island in the Marshall Islands, one specific instance of this kind of island.

clue.text: Victim of robbery by The Pearly Queen?

definitions.text: Victim of robbery by The Pearly Queen?

parts.words: Victim of robbery by The Pearly Queen?
parts.note: surface reading: someone robbed by a Pearly Queen, a London charity figure in a pearl-button costume; setter's reading: whoever wears pearls has taken them from the shellfish that grew them

explanation.walkthrough: Pearly Kings and Queens are Cockney charity figures who wear clothes covered in pearl buttons; the joke is that pearls are taken from a shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearls form inside certain bivalve molluscs, so harvesting one means robbing the creature that made it.

clue.text: A sharpness of tongue, funny: RIP Yeats

indicators.note: something funny is odd or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued, comic epitaph for the Irish poet W. B. Yeats.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'A' belongs to the definition, not the letters to be mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Asperity is harshness of tone or manner, especially cutting remarks, which is what a sharp tongue delivers.
